extracted.intended_audience: British newspaper readers, Parliament watchers and policymakers interested in wartime developments
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report summarizing Prime Minister Churchill's war review and related wartime policy statements delivered in the House of Commons. Covers military situation, allied command, censorship, resistance movements, and post‑liberation political principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commander nationality follows majority of troops
rubrics_metrics.description: The nationality of the commander should in general follow the majority of troops in any theater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to justify allied command arrangements (e.g., appointing commanders such as Eisenhower or Alexander where the majority of forces were of a given nationality). Principle for assigning supreme command in multinational operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge parties by readiness to fight the Germans
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge all parties and factions dispassionately by the test of their readiness and ability to fight the Germans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political/operational support decisions should be based on practical willingness and ability to oppose the enemy rather than ideological preference; referenced in decisions about support for forces in Yugoslavia, Greece, and Italy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep good faith with those who kept good faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep good faith with those who have kept good faith with us and strive without prejudice to aid those who strike for freedom against Nazi rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guiding principle in relations with governments-in-exile, resistance movements and liberated countries; implies honoring commitments to allies and partisans who cooperated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeds not words
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a time for deeds and not words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes prioritizing concrete military action and practical measures over rhetoric or political point-scoring, especially during critical phases of the campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid alarmist language in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Such words as ‘desperate’ ought not to be used in a battle of this kind when they are false and still less are they to be used if they are true.’ If false they distress the public; if true they encourage the enemy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification for tighter censorship on alarmist or sensational reporting; guidance for correspondents and editors to avoid headlines/phrases that either unduly alarm the public or give the enemy advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance press liberty with troop safety
rubrics_metrics.description: The liberty of the press is of high consequence; so also are the lives of our troops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press freedom is valued but may be constrained when reporting risks soldiers' lives or operational security; actions (temporary restrictions, censorship) may be justified to protect forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff appointments by merit regardless of nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff positions should be filled with whoever is thought to be the best man and operate without regard to country, with officers ordering each other according to rank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model of allied staff cooperation exemplified by Eisenhower's uniform staff in Africa; encourages meritocratic, integrated allied command structures rather than national siloing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-liberation governments decided when stable and by the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Greece, Yugoslavia and Italy will be perfectly free to settle the forms which their governments shall take once the will of the people can be obtained under conditions of tranquillity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imposing political systems prematurely; review and arrange political settlements only after military conditions (e.g., capture of Rome) and stability allow free expression of the people's will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'unconditional surrender'
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Unconditional surrender’ does not mean the German people will be enslaved or destroyed; it means the Allies will not be bound to them at the moment of surrender by any pact or obligation (e.g., Atlantic Charter will not apply to Germany as of right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies the legal/political scope of surrender terms and the Allies' freedom to make post-war arrangements; counters misconceptions about unconditional surrender implying collective punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aid to resistance based on effectiveness against the enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: Support and aid should be given to resistance forces that are effectively fighting the Germans (e.g., Tito’s Partisans are described as the only force doing effective fighting in Yugoslavia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical criterion for allocating missions, supplies and backing: effectiveness in inflicting losses on the occupier and maintaining resistance under reprisals; resources constrained by other obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with enemy undermines legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Forces or commanders who make accommodations with the enemy (e.g., elements associated with General Mihailovic) lose claim to support and legitimacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of commanders whose failure to act or collaboration reduced their standing; implication that continued or substantial collaboration disqualifies groups from Allied backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make premature political changes in liberated countries
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be a mistake to suppose that the political conditions exist in Italy for normal political processes; review political position only after military entry into Rome and when material conditions (food, shipping) permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay major political restructuring until military and logistical realities are addressed; avoid unsettling changes that could hamper cooperation with allied armies.

rubrics_metrics.name: High command should issue frequent authoritative statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The high command on the spot should issue more frequent and authoritative statements to prevent wrong impressions arising from secondary or rear-area sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authoritative military communiqués to counter misinformation and reduce the need for censorship; the Prime Minister supplemented such statements and requested tighter control on alarmist reports from Naples/Algiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint land-sea-air operations are imperative
rubrics_metrics.description: The war effort requires coordinated action by land, sea and air; the plan is to strike the enemy by land, sea and air with all available strength in the coming spring and summer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic imperative for synchronized multi-domain campaigns (e.g., amphibious landings supported by artillery, armor and air power); operational planning should account for weather, terrain and enemy reinforcements.
